To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the optimal interfacing of a GHz-bandwidth, on-demand heralded single-photon source to a Raman-type, broadband quantum memory is achieved by using a source with a 1.2 nm-wide spectrum centered on 852 nm, a 1.8 nm FWHM linewidth, and 0.3 dBm power.
we interfaced a heralded single photon sources to a Raman memory, and we optimized the source characteristics to match the memory bandwidth.
we have interfaced a R&D-level quantum memory and heralded single photon sources, demonstrating the first passive stability and on-demand re-emission of heralded single photons from a Cs memory.

the development of quantum technologies based on the interaction of single photons with matter.
the development of new technologies for the production of entangled photon pairs and their application in quantum optics experiments.
the development of a deterministic source for a scalable quantum network.

we are now in a position to perform quantum logic gates with our source, and we are currently testing the performance of the source in a quantum repeater experiment.

the source is not only compatible with the memory, but that it can be optimised to match the memory bandwidth, and that it can be interfaced with the memory without active stabilisation.
